fixture_name: Cloverleaf-to-urban interchange conversion — INT preliminary design (Wikimedia PD geometry)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Shortened collector-distributor weave carrying a recorded 1,100 pcu/h design-year flow concentrates lane-change demand between residual loop and terminal traffic, a recognised sideswipe/rear-end mechanism squarely relevant at preliminary design before geometry is fixed.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal normative claim is anchored in a verbatim EV-IN-015 quote covering junction-type suitability for traffic volume/movements, stream channelling, lane balance and through-lane continuity, with EV-IN-004 confirming preliminary-design stage applicability and the reduced-length weave and 1,100 pcu/h stated as recorded inputs; no invented content detected beyond a benign unverified §10.2 label.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Maintained as a safety_concern with a distinct verification pathway (checklist prompts, HSM/IHSDM evaluation) rather than a compliance assertion, correctly staged at int:preliminary-design so the issue is raised before detailed design locks in the weave geometry.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and tiered: apply the cited PIARC prompts, quantify adequacy via HSM Part C interchange models or IHSDM evaluation, then either lengthen the weave or add entry ramp metering if flagged — actionable and viable at preliminary design.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU impacts are explicitly considered and scoped out: shared-use paths are grade-separated from the motorised weaving section, so vehicle occupants-only scoping is justified and the non-applicability is clearly acknowledged.

justifications.substance: Uncontrolled free-flow ramp-terminal crossings conflicting with retained shared-use paths is a substantive preliminary-design safety issue directly tied to the recorded objective of improved pedestrian/cycle continuity across the corridor.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (PIARC requirement for pedestrian/cyclist provision at junctions) is backed by a verbatim quote in EV-IN-016, reinforced by EV-IN-005's verbatim all-road-users/thematic-audit text, while the scheme-specific layout and objective claims are presented as recorded input facts.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed as a safety_concern within the qualified PIARC preliminary-design baseline; the checklist prompts serve as corroboration while the hazard (uncontrolled VRU crossings) remains the operative concern, keeping compliance questions categorically distinct.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: named PIARC pedestrian-audit tools (Walkability Checklist, CQSI), defined treatment types (signalised or grade-separated), and identified locations at both retained loop-ramp terminals including the northern path crossing.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are the explicit focus of the finding, with their exposure at ramp-terminal crossings analysed as the core risk pathway.
